purpose: Reconcile the two McNemar pooling methods used in verdict.json and mcnemar_pairwise_and_doc.json
prereg_verbatim: pooled McNemar exact two-sided p < 0.01 with net delta > 0
prereg_note: The prereg says 'pooled McNemar' but does not specify concatenation vs Cartesian pairing. Both methods are therefore admissible under the protocol text.

method_A_concat.description: Concatenate all rec-seed corr_worst arrays (2 seeds x 5000 = 10,000) and all ff-seed corr_worst arrays (3 seeds x 5000 = 15,000). Truncate ff to 10,000 (min of the two). Compute 2x2 discordant table on the 10,000 paired observations.
method_A_concat.pseudo_replication: Each image appears once per seed. rec17 images are paired with ff17 images (position 0-4999), rec42 with ff42 (position 5000-9999). The pairing is arbitrary — rec17 images could equally be paired with ff42.

method_B_cartesian.description: For each of the 6 (rec_seed, ff_seed) pairs, compute per-image discordant counts on the same 5,000 validation images. Sum b and c across all 6 pairs. N = 2 x 3 x 5000 = 30,000.
method_B_cartesian.pseudo_replication: Each image is counted 6 times (once per seed pair). This inflates n_discordant and deflates p-values. Not valid for seed-level inference.

reconciliation.difference_explanation: Different pooling: concat (10k) vs Cartesian (30k). Both pseudo-replicated. Direction agrees (ff > rec). Magnitude differs (−2.01 vs −1.84 pp) because concat pairs rec17 with ff17 by position, while Cartesian averages all 6 cross-seed comparisons including the 3 rec42-vs-ff pairs where rec42 wins.
reconciliation.verdict_decided_by: min-rule: min(rec_112) = 30.18% < min(ff_112) = 35.44%. McNemar was descriptive only.

caveats: Neither method provides valid seed-level inference. With 2 and 3 seeds, there is no meaningful seed-level test.
The statement 'seed 42 is significantly superior' is a statement about one checkpoint on 5,000 images, and seed 42 is the better of two seeds (selection bias).
p-values should not be quoted as evidence of a seed-level effect. They are descriptive summaries of image-level discordance.
